name: Softr
tagline: No-code portals and internal apps on Airtable/Google Sheets and databases

pricing.notes: Official pricing/docs checked 2026-07-30; Basic listed at $59/month monthly and $49/month annually.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Up to 3 builders; 5 total app users; free workspace/app limits
tiers.notes: A 7-day Business trial is separate from the permanent Free plan.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 1 builder; 5 team users + 5 client users; 1 custom domain
tiers.notes: Extra builders cost $6 monthly or $5/month on annual billing.

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.notes: Extra team users are $3/month up to 50; extra client users are $1/month up to 250.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.notes: Extra team users are $5/month up to 100; extra client users are $2/month up to 500.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom builders, users, security, support and contract terms

pricing.freeTierCaps: Up to 3 builders and 5 total app users
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; annual pricing is lower, while user overages are still calculated and billed monthly
pricing.hiddenCosts: Extra builders, users and domains are separately billed: extra domains are $15/month or $13/month on annual billing; users are counted daily with a 7-day grace period and no mid-cycle refund; workflow caps can pause automations, and AI credits reset without rollover

verdictSummary: A client portal over Airtable can be built, but Softr's block library, auth, roles, data sources, payments, and publishing workflow are the product.
coreLoopDIY: Build a CRUD portal with auth, role-gated pages, list/detail views, forms, and Airtable/Postgres backing data.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay so non-engineers can launch portals without hiring a developer.

priorArt.name: Budibase
priorArt.desc: Open-source low-code platform for internal tools and portals.

alternatives.name: Baserow Free
alternatives.desc: The database and app builder live together; portals are less polished, but forms, roles, views, and external users are present.

facts.dataFormat: Tables, application definitions, uploads, and workspace metadata live in Baserow Cloud; tables can be exported as CSV
facts.gapVsPaid: Baserow's app pages are markedly less polished and template-rich for branded client portals than Softr's responsive block library.

alternatives.name: Budibase
alternatives.desc: Internal apps, forms, automations, and portals in one box; much closer to Knack than its developer branding suggests.

facts.install: Docker image or Docker Compose; Kubernetes is also supported
facts.engines: Model-agnostic; the agent builder supports bring-your-own AI provider credentials
facts.dataFormat: Built-in app data and app definitions are stored in CouchDB, files in MinIO/S3-compatible object storage, and connected external data remains in its source system
facts.gapVsPaid: Its internal-tool aesthetic and component system are less suitable for polished public portals, directories, and membership sites than Softr.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires Docker and persistent storage; production use also means owning upgrades, TLS, backups, and database/network access

alternatives.name: NocoBase
alternatives.desc: A database-backed app builder with pages, forms, roles, workflows, and enough plugins to become your next maintenance hobby.

facts.install: NocoBase CLI or Docker deployment with MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL
facts.engines: Built-in AI employees can connect to common LLMs; exact provider support depends on installed AI plugins
facts.dataFormat: Business data lives in standard relational tables in the configured MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL database; files use configured local or object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: NocoBase trades Softr's hosted visual page building and templates for self-hosted database administration and a more technical plugin model.
facts.setupBlocker: Requires a database, secrets, and deployment administration; the community license also preserves NocoBase branding and restricts some uses

alternatives.name: REI3
alternatives.desc: A sober business-app builder with forms, reports, roles, workflows, and no per-user meter.

facts.install: Native Linux/Windows server package or Docker Compose, connected to PostgreSQL
facts.dataFormat: Human-readable application records and configuration live in a PostgreSQL database controlled by the operator
facts.gapVsPaid: REI3 can build functional role-aware apps, but its visual design, templates, and external portal experience are much more utilitarian than Softr.
facts.setupBlocker: You must provision PostgreSQL and configure a server/reverse proxy; it is not a managed one-click workspace

alternatives.name: Softr Free
alternatives.desc: The same product's free plan publishes one branded portal with internal and external users, data actions, forms, and workflows.

facts.dataFormat: App definitions and any Softr Database records live in Softr's cloud; connected-source records remain in the external source, with Softr proxying requests and caching data for up to 24 hours; table blocks can export CSV or XLSX
facts.gapVsPaid: It is the same builder, but the free plan keeps Softr branding and materially tighter limits on published apps, users, records, and advanced controls.
facts.setupBlocker: No software install; the first hurdle is choosing and authenticating a data source, then mapping its fields and permissions

notes: Useful for the no-code replacement category: yes for a custom portal, kinda for the platform.
prompt:
Build me a client portal to replace Softr: one portal for my own clients, not a portal
builder. Requirements:

- Node + Express + nunjucks, server-rendered; data stays in Airtable via its REST API
  (base ID and token in .env) so records keep being edited there.
- Magic-link login: a client enters their email, gets a signed link via Resend (secret
  in .env); sessions in signed cookies. Allowed emails live in an Airtable Clients
  table.
- Each client sees only rows linked to their client record: a list view with the columns
  named in views.json, and a detail view per record.
- One submission form that appends a row to a chosen table, with file upload passed
  through to Airtable attachments.
- A role flag on the client record (client vs admin); admins see all rows.
- Cache Airtable reads for 60 seconds to stay under rate limits.
- Runs on my VPS behind HTTPS; no telemetry, no third parties beyond Airtable and the
  email sender.
- Out of scope: a drag-and-drop page builder, payments, and memberships. Pages are
  defined in config files, that is the builder.
- README: Airtable token scopes, expected table and field names, and email sender setup.
